The CBO's nonpartisan analysis projects 7.8 million losing Medicaid under the One Big Beautiful Bill - far beyond the 4.8 million "able-bodied" figure being floated. This discrepancy stems from provisions like Section 44101's punitive work reporting mandates and Section 44122's retroactive coverage cuts from 3 months to 1. The bill's 1,000-page rushed structure creates bureaucratic tripwires that will boot low-income workers, disabled Americans, and caregivers from coverage even if technically eligible.

While the intent to streamline spending is valid, the execution fails basic accountability - it's like trying to fix a leaky faucet with a sledgehammer.

Real reform requires DOGE-style audits targeting $200B in annual Medicaid fraud by hospitals and pharma middlemen, not stripping coverage from vulnerable citizens caught in red tape.

The Biden-era staffing mandate was classic D.C. overreach—a rigid, one-size-fits-all disaster that ignored rural realities. The Big Beautiful Bill (H.R.1) rightly axes this bureaucratic straitjacket, restoring local control so facilities can prioritize patient needs over checkbox compliance. North Dakota’s nursing homes shouldn’t drown in red tape while trying to care for veterans and farmers.

This repeal aligns with Trump’s broader push to slash suffocating regulations, redirecting resources from compliance officers to bedside care.

Rural America needs tailored solutions, not D.C. mandates crafted by urban bureaucrats who’ve never set foot in a heartland care facility.
